description: The website and CLI share this saved 3D game creation workflow. Ask which engine (Unity, Godot, Unreal, Three.js) if unspecified; do not choose silently. create saves a brief without spending. quote(operation=plan) estimates AI preparation (player_accounts=true adds player accounts through central.client even to a solo game; off by default, online multiplayer always has it), accept(quote_token) starts its durable job ONLY after user approval of the shown price. get returns a persistent operation log, slots, studio_url and the same project to resume. Planning can select an appropriate preset OR compose real engine-compatible modules. A missing preset never means the genre needs a native engine. composition.modules pins all module versions; composition.tasks lists the custom logic still to implement. New plans return design from a separate game-designer agent: named content lists and their counts, animation clips per actor, user-request versus agent-proposal attribution, assumptions and a machine-readable completion contract. Show this saved scope before assembly; refine changes it. get also returns production_sources. quote(operation=produce, production_source=one source ID) estimates a bounded production batch for any contract content, animation, capability or journey obligation; omit production_source to choose the next unprepared source. After price approval, accept runs decomposition, compatible Library matching, authored source documents and at most one concept board for missing visual assets, cropped into individually traceable review drafts. Audio, animation and executable VFX never become complete through a picture. An unavailable matcher with candidates requires review rather than speculative replacement. production.batches persists tasks, dependencies, acceptance checks, candidates, concepts, text, deferred work and diagnostics. asset_matched is not acquisition or integration. draft_ready is not gameplay verification. Changed design fingerprints retain old batches as stale. Use existing concept review/manufacturing and content tools for integration; Develop can read production batches using creation_production. Never report prepared-source coverage as game completeness. Assembly persists that contract on the project before auditing. A design is not implementation or passing evidence. The quoted planning budget includes this bounded stage; old accepted jobs retain their original behavior. New plans also return world: structure (open_world, semi_open, linear, arena, interior or circuit), deterministic seed, validated kit configurations, level documents and remaining work. Assembly applies this saved layout atomically. Reuse it when continuing in the CLI; a visual-theme change does not imply changing geography. A seed change alone is not a designed level. Show world.remaining, including unbuilt architecture or transitions, before calling the game complete. Assembly is a foundation, not a completed custom game: For contract-backed web games, quote build includes a persistent queue derived from every named source and capability, with isolated authoring sessions and independent final verification; there is no twelve-turn limit for the entire game. Review the quoted maximum before acceptance. Unattempted credit-funded tasks are not charged. development.work records reported_unverified and blocked tasks, retained authoring IDs and pending IDs; these are not release evidence. delivery.status=ready requires the build-specific contract and final checks. For an assembled project, quote operation=develop with an optional message to continue the saved queue under a new approved budget, preserving the same project and completed authoring work. The development result distinguishes agent-declared changes, actual checks, remaining work and unsupported runtime capabilities. Each additional pass needs its own estimate. When the contract requires a HUD, new build/develop quotes expose interface_preparation: they reuse the saved concept or include one bounded HUD concept generation and editable document. Its price is included; accepted older quotes never add it. Read creation_hud during authoring, implement the game data in its presenter and use the existing gripforge_hud runtime artistic review. A concept alone does not complete the HUD. Other asset generation requires its own quoted stage. Native/custom-code development still uses the CLI. After a build, get also returns creatures (the models bound so that no unit is a capsule) and audit { verdict: complete | playable_with_defects | incomplete, headline, fixed (the free fixes applied: models, standard clips, control scheme), defects [{ severity, message, fix { tool, args, credits? } }], next }: show the user the verdict and what is left, work through next (gripforge_game_audit reads it again), and never present a verdict other than complete as a finished game. quote refine with message updates the same plan after approval, preserves selected assets and reviewed work, and persists the conversation. use_reference with slot_id and an owned image asset_id supplies an uploaded concept for visual review. assets searches workspace/community items by actual role before invented generation details. Generic nature packs may cross world themes while keeping the rendering look. New plans consider available styles before inventing one; selection_reason explains planner choices. other_styles=true reveals alternatives with explicit mismatch/unknown compatibility for manual review; never bind a known look mismatch automatically. Prefer reuse before generation; select chooses one or sets mode=generate with a prompt. For generation: quote concept, obtain approval, accept, poll get, show the concept, approve_concept only after visual user review; quote generate, obtain approval, accept, poll and show the model in its studio. A quote with auto_select_character=true selects the missing main character by default when ready; it remains inspectable and replaceable. Other models, replacement generations and older approved jobs remain drafts: approve_asset only after visual review. Never infer visual approval from technical success. quote build then accept acquires the selected community assets and binds them to a Game Kit prototype; generated artwork and models must appear in the accepted quote. The main playable character is presented first. If no usable matching rigged/animated model is found, prepare its generation. A missing main character blocks assembly until an existing or generated model is selected. With explicit allow_incomplete=true on the build quote, missing secondary slots may use module defaults where available or remain empty, but a generated model awaiting review blocks assembly until explicitly approved or another asset is selected. Show missing_assets before approval; never imply that an incomplete prototype is finished. Native engine projects still need CLI delivery/import; a web project has a play_url. Revision required for edits. Every get, list item and action response carries status: idle | running | failed | cancelled | ready, with status_detail { job_id, operation, job_status, stage, message, actions }. Poll get while status=running; stop on failed or cancelled, show status_detail.message and offer the listed actions (retry, dismiss). pending alone never means in progress: a failed job stays pending until retried or dismissed. Cancel/retry preserve completed steps. 2D unsupported. No automatic spending, invented asset IDs, or unrelated template substitutions.
name: gripforge_game_creation
title: Prepare and resume a game
